properties.content: Question: sentinel bleed symptoms Answer: A sentinel bleed, also known as a warning leak, is a minor bleed from a brain aneurysm that can precede a more serious subarachnoid hemorrhage. Symptoms often include a sudden, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to light (photophobia), and neck pain. These symptoms can appear hours or even weeks before a full rupture. Here's a more detailed breakdown:: - Sudden, Severe Headache: This is often described as the "worst headache of my life" and can come on very quickly. - Nausea and Vomiting: The increased pressure in the brain can trigger these symptoms. - Photophobia: Sensitivity to light is another common symptom, likely due to irritation of the meninges (membranes surrounding the brain). - Malaise: General feeling of discomfort, illness, or unease. - Neck Pain: Pain and stiffness in the neck can also occur. - Other Potential Symptoms: Some people may experience vision changes, confusion, or changes in consciousness. - Sentinel vs. Rupture: It's crucial to note that while sentinel bleeds are a warning sign, they can also be a sign of an impending rupture. If you experience any of these symptoms, seek immediate medical attention.
